subsystems.name: Cell source and expansion
subsystems.role: provides the living building blocks: muscle and fat cells taken from an animal biopsy and multiplied in bioreactors.
parts: growth medium with nutrients and growth factors

subsystems.name: Bioink formulation
subsystems.role: turns cells into a printable material that keeps them alive and guides their arrangement.

subsystems.name: Bioprinter
subsystems.role: deposits the bioink in precise layers to build whole-cut structures.

subsystems.name: Edible scaffold
subsystems.role: supports the printed layers and encourages cells to align into fibres, mimicking the texture of meat.
parts: textured plant protein (e.g. soy or pea)

subsystems.name: Maturation bioreactor
subsystems.role: keeps the printed construct warm, oxygenated and fed so the cells fuse and develop texture and flavour.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: turns the matured construct into a food product.

buildSteps.title: Isolate cells
buildSteps.detail: A small, harmless biopsy is taken from a living animal and muscle and fat stem cells are separated out.

buildSteps.title: Expand the cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells are grown in bioreactors at 37 °C in a nutrient broth, doubling every day or so until billions are available.

buildSteps.title: Mix the bioink
buildSteps.detail: Cells are combined with an edible hydrogel or plant-protein base to form a paste that can be extruded without killing them.

buildSteps.title: Print the structure
buildSteps.detail: A bioprinter lays down alternating layers of muscle and fat ink, building up a 3D shape layer by layer, often just fractions of a millimetre thick.

buildSteps.title: Insert scaffold
buildSteps.detail: An edible, porous scaffold is placed between or within layers to give the structure mechanical support and to align cells into fibres.

buildSteps.title: Mature the construct
buildSteps.detail: The printed piece is moved to a bioreactor where it is perfused with oxygen and nutrients for days or weeks, letting cells fuse and form texture.

buildSteps.title: Finish and package
buildSteps.detail: The matured meat is cooked, shaped, and packed under refrigeration for distribution.

prerequisites.why: growing cells cheaply at high density is the main cost barrier; current processes are far from food-industry scale.
scaffolds and hydrogels must be food-safe, support cell growth, and not spoil the taste or texture.
printing one steak is slow; industrial output needs many print heads working in parallel.
getting oxygen and nutrients into pieces thicker than a few millimetres without a blood vessel network is unsolved.
a few countries have approved small-scale sales, but rules for printed whole cuts are still being written.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale demonstrations of 3D-printed meat pieces a few centimetres across
pathway.unlocks: proof that cells can survive printing and mature into textured tissue.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants producing kilogram quantities for tasting and early sales
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on cost, safety and consumer acceptance.

pathway.milestone: scaffolds and bioreactors that let thick cuts mature without a vascular network
pathway.unlocks: whole cuts such as steak or fillet rather than minced or shredded products.

pathway.milestone: industrial-scale printing lines integrated with cheap, food-grade growth media
pathway.unlocks: cultivated meat at prices competitive with conventional meat, with far less land and water use.
